basic_details.short_information: IIT Kharagpur has one opening for a Project Research Scientist - I (Non-Medical). The post is in an ICMR-funded research project in the Department of Medical Science and Technology. The project uses machine learning and multi-omics data to tell lymph node tuberculosis apart from sarcoidosis. The job pays a consolidated amount of up to Rs. 56000 a month. There is no application fee. Online applications close on 12 November 2026.

age_limit.details: Candidates who have worked in a Government Research Organization may be given up to 5 years of age relaxation. The DG, ICMR or the Head of the Institution decides this case by case. Age rules may also be relaxed under the sponsoring agency's rules, if there are any. | Meeting the minimum qualifications and experience does not guarantee a call for interview. Check the official notification for the full eligibility for this post.

content_sections.text: Post Graduate Degree, including the integrated PG degrees For Engineering / IT / CS - Four Years Graduate Degree At least 1 year of research experience in respiratory health and machine learning, with publications in the relevant area. This experience is preferred but not essential. Candidates who have worked in a Government Research Organization may be given up to 5 years of age relaxation. content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: The notice says that applicants will be called for an interview. Meeting the minimum qualifications and experience alone does not guarantee an interview call.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: This is a temporary post in a purely time-bound research project. Tenure: 36 months or until the project ends, whichever is earlier. The first contract is for up to one year. It can be extended up to three years, depending on need and a performance review by the PI/Director. In exceptional cases, the Director General, ICMR may extend it up to five years, depending on the nature and needs of the project. The fixed-term engagement, whether the first term or an extension, ends automatically if it is not extended within the tenure. Extensions cannot be given retrospectively.

faq.question: Q1. Who is funding this project post?
faq.answer: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), New Delhi, sponsors the project. Its project code is R/OIG.

faq.question: Q2. Can engineering graduates apply?
faq.answer: Yes. Candidates from Engineering / IT / CS need a four-year graduate degree. Others need a Post Graduate Degree, and integrated PG degrees count.

faq.question: Q3. Is research experience compulsory?
faq.answer: No. It is listed as desired experience: at least 1 year of research in respiratory health and machine learning, with publications in the area.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit, and on which date is age counted?
faq.answer: The limit is 40 years. Age is counted as on the last date of the advertisement, which is 12 November 2026.

faq.question: Q5. Is there age relaxation for experienced candidates?
faq.answer: Yes. Candidates who have worked in a Government Research Organization may get up to 5 years of relaxation. The DG, ICMR or the Head of the Institution decides each case.

faq.question: Q6. Is HRA paid on top of the salary?
faq.answer: Yes. HRA is paid as admissible, on top of the consolidated pay of up to Rs. 56000 a month. The exact pay depends on qualification and experience.

faq.question: Q7. How long will the job last?
faq.answer: The tenure is 36 months or until the project ends, whichever is earlier. The first contract is for up to one year and can be extended after a performance review.

faq.question: Q8. Who is the Principal Investigator for this project?
faq.answer: The PI/Co-PI is Prof./Dr. Koel Chaudhury of the Department of Medical Science and Technology, IIT Kharagpur.
